_README: Week-by-week STARTING schedules for a new medicine (add or switch), copied VERBATIM from Dr. Barbour's '<Drug> Initiation' tabs. Cells are text exactly as she wrote them; '—' means no tablet schedule fits (use the liquid). The engine only DISPLAYS these to the clinician; it never computes or changes a dose from them. DRAFT - verified:false, pending PI sign-off.
source: clinician (Barbour final_doses_titration_v9.xlsx, '<Drug> Initiation' tabs; built by data/_build_initiation_schedules.py)

notes: Levetiracetam — Initiation titration by weight
Dosed twice daily. Steps go 10, 20, then 30 mg/kg/day and stop. If needed, keep titrating toward the maintenance range in the last column.
Week 1 is at or below 10 mg/kg/day. Each weekly increase stays within 10 mg/kg/day (plus 10%). Every band’s final step is checked against the 10%-below / 30%-above window around 30 mg/kg/day.
Solution 100 mg/mL, split evenly AM/PM, measured to 0.1 mL under 5 mL and whole mL from 5 mL. Tablets 250 / 500 / 750 / 1000 mg, one strength per band, whole or half. Schedules end on whole tablets.
A dash means no tablet schedule fits that band, so use the solution.
Clobazam — Initiation titration by weight group
Clobazam is dosed by weight group with fixed doses (not mg/kg). The ≥ 50 kg row keeps going to 10 mg twice daily, so it ends on whole tablets.

Week 1 is a single dose at night. From week 2 the dose is split twice daily. Each weekly increase is 5 mg/day or less (Lexicomp: no more often than every 5 days). Titrate further toward the maintenance range as tolerated.
Oral solution 2.5 mg/mL; tablets 10 / 20 mg (scored, halve to 5 mg).
Doses under 20 kg (2.5–5 mg) are too small to divide from a 10 mg tablet, so the oral solution is used.

notes: Brivaracetam — Initiation (started directly, no gradual titration)
Brivaracetam needs no gradual titration — start at the dose shown, twice daily, then adjust within the maintenance range.
Dose is the top of the Lexicomp starting range at the band midpoint, rounded down: up to 3 mg/kg/day under 11 kg, 2.5 from 11–20 kg, 2 from 20–50 kg, and 100 mg/day from 50 kg.

Oral solution 10 mg/mL, split evenly AM/PM and measured to 0.1 mL. Tablets 10 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 100 mg (not scored), one strength per band, whole tablets only, one tablet per dose where Lexicomp’s starting range allows. A dash means no tablet dose fits, so use the solution.
Lexicomp maximum daily doses: 6 mg/kg/day under 11 kg, 5 from 11–20 kg, 4 from 20–50 kg, 200 mg/day from 50 kg.
Ethosuximide — Initiation titration by weight
Twice-daily. Titrate weekly: 10 → 15 → 20 mg/kg/day; 20 mg/kg (Week 3) is the maintenance floor and the dose target.
Optimal window is 10% below to 30% above each week's target mg/kg; amber marks a band/step outside it.
Oral solution 50 mg/mL, split evenly AM/PM (half mL under 5 mL). Capsules are 250 mg and not splittable, so smaller doses that aren't a whole-capsule twice-daily amount use the solution.
Weight-dosed to 50 kg; from 50 kg the dose holds at the 50 kg amount (500 / 750 / 1000 mg/day), the adult dose. Maintenance range 20–30 mg/kg/day (max 2,000 mg/day).
Valproic acid — Initiation titration by weight
Titrate weekly 10 → 15 → 20 → 25 → 30 mg/kg/day; 30 mg/kg (Week 5) is the maintenance floor and the dose target.
Optimal window is 10% below to 30% above the Week 5 target mg/kg; amber marks a band outside it.

Oral solution 50 mg/mL (even AM/PM, half mL under 5 mL). Immediate-release tablets 125 / 250 / 500 mg (whole); doses with no clean tablet amount use the solution. Extended-release tablets exist for once-daily maintenance.
Weight-dosed to 50 kg; from 50 kg the dose holds at the 50 kg amount (adult). Maintenance range 30–60 mg/kg/day (max 3,000 mg/day).
Zonisamide — Initiation titration by weight / age

Children: dose by weight (mg/kg); adults (>16 y) use the fixed schedule in the last row. The solution is given twice daily throughout; a small Week-1 tablet/capsule dose may be given once daily (shown in each cell).
Columns are the weekly titration steps the tool defines (child steps 1 → 3.5 mg/kg/day); keep titrating toward the maintenance range in the last column.
Only the final shown step is checked against the 10%-below / 30%-above window; amber marks a band outside it. Oral suspension 20 mg/mL (even AM/PM, half mL under 5 mL).
Capsules 25 / 50 / 100 mg are not splittable, so weeks with no clean whole-capsule twice-daily amount show a dash — use the suspension.
Lacosamide — Initiation titration by weight
Twice-daily throughout. Under 50 kg dose by weight (mg/kg); at 50 kg and above use the fixed adult schedule in the last row.

Columns are weekly steps: 1.5, 3, 4.5, 6 mg/kg/day under 30 kg, and 1, 2, 3, 4 mg/kg/day for 30–50 kg. Both end at the bottom of the Lexicomp maintenance range. Continue toward the range in the last column if needed.
Every band’s final step is checked against the 10%-below / 30%-above window. Oral solution 10 mg/mL, split evenly AM/PM, measured to 0.1 mL under 5 mL and 0.5 mL from 5 mL.

Tablets 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 mg, whole or half; schedules end on whole tablets. Tablet steps may go up to the Lexicomp increment of 2 mg/kg/day, so they can differ from the solution. A dash means use the solution.
Topiramate — Initiation titration by weight group
Dosed by weight group with fixed milligram amounts (not mg/kg). Under 38 kg, week 1 is given once daily at night, then twice daily from week 2. Over 38 kg, doses are twice daily from week 1.
Columns are the weekly titration steps; keep increasing weekly toward the maintenance range shown in the last column.
Oral solution 25 mg/mL. Tablets and sprinkle capsules 15 / 25 / 50 / 100 / 200 mg (whole); a week with no clean twice-daily tablet amount shows a dash — use the solution or sprinkle capsules.
Titrate slowly (weekly) to limit cognitive and tingling side effects. Extended-release once-daily capsules also exist.
Oxcarbazepine — Initiation titration by weight

Under 20 kg dose by weight (mg/kg); at 20 kg and above use the fixed weight-group schedules. The suspension is given twice daily throughout; a Week-1 tablet dose may be given once daily (shown in each cell).
Columns are the weekly titration steps; keep increasing weekly toward the maintenance range shown in the last column.

Oral suspension 60 mg/mL, split evenly AM/PM and measured to 0.1 mL (whole mL at 5 mL and up). Tablets 150 / 300 / 600 mg, whole or half. Schedules always end on whole tablets. A dash means no tablet dose fits that week, so use the suspension.
Every band’s final step is checked against the 10%-below / 30%-above window.
Lamotrigine — Initiation titration (slow; not on valproate or enzyme inducers)
Titrate lamotrigine slowly. Rushing raises the risk of serious rash. This schedule is for patients not on valproate and not on enzyme-inducing drugs, which need different, lower dosing.

Children dose by weight. Weeks 1–2: 0.3 mg/kg/day, once daily. Weeks 3–4: 0.6 mg/kg/day, twice daily. Then increase weekly by up to 0.6 mg/kg/day (no more than 25 mg/day) until about 4.5 mg/kg/day. Adolescents and adults: 25 mg/day for weeks 1–2, 50 mg/day for weeks 3–4, then 50 mg/day more each week to 250 mg/day.

Suspension 10 mg/mL, measured to 0.1 mL under 5 mL and to 0.5 mL from 5 mL. Tablets may be halved, but every schedule ends on whole tablets. Many children start on 5 mg tablets and switch to 25 mg tablets once the dose allows, so they need both prescriptions.
Every band’s final step is checked against the 10%-below / 30%-above window. Schedules run 8 to 14 weeks. After that, keep titrating toward the maintenance range in the last column.
